title: Build, test and protect a dashboard an owner can trust

say: Build, test and protect a dashboard an owner can trust.
This is the video for module two of Advanced Excel and Dashboards.
Most dashboards are fed by exports from a POS system, a bank or accounting software. Cleaning them by hand every month is slow, and it is where errors creep in.

say: Create a Checks area. Each check compares two numbers that must agree, and the difference should be 0.
Ada's source Table adds up to 18,912,500 naira, but the dashboard shows 18,600,000.
The gap is 312,500. The pivot pointed to a fixed range, so 5 late invoices of 62,500 each were left out. She points the pivot at tblSales, refreshes, and the check returns 0.
Add data validation to input cells, unlock only those cells, then protect the sheet. Test that the slicers still work. But sheet protection only prevents accidents.
For salaries, customer details or bank information, use Encrypt with Password, with a strong password sent through a different channel.
Exports often hold customer names and phone numbers. Remove columns you do not need, and never forward raw exports on personal WhatsApp.
Before you send the file, tick every item. Test with awkward data on purpose: a blank quantity, a date typed as text, a duplicate invoice.
Do not hide errors with IFERROR and a zero, because a broken lookup then looks like a real zero.
Finally, write a How It Works sheet and ask someone else to follow it without your help.

panel.heading: Handover checklist
items: Totals reconcile to source
Row counts match exports
Blank and odd inputs tested
Formula cells locked
How It Works sheet written

say: Automate an import from a folder of at least three files. Build your one-screen dashboard with cards, charts and a connected slicer. Then add check cells, protect it and write the How It Works sheet.
